messages:
raj: Heads-up — we're rotating the customer-data keystore keys tomorrow 03:00 UTC. This rotation will remove old service-account decrypt rights and add a new ephemeral SA. Anyone see DSAR / deletion-proof fallout?
jen: Which key alias exactly? alias/customer-data-prod?
raj: yep. alias/customer-data-prod. Concern: the deletion/proof pipeline needs to decrypt archived blobs to generate proof packages for subject requests. If it loses decrypt perms mid-rotate we could fail proofs.
mike: If decrypt fails we can't produce evidence for legal SLOs. We need a short mitigation plan.
sara: From legal: we can tolerate a short, pre-announced freeze if we export pending proofs first and keep an audit trail. Need to make sure KMS audit events are available.
raj: keystore-proxy currently emits structured events on deny: `keystore.decrypt_denied` with principal and object id. Deletion service treats decrypt exceptions as transient and defers retries. That won't help for DSAR proofs that expect timely receipts.
jen: Proposal: 1) run pre-rotation export for any pending proof jobs (48h window), 2) grant a timebound `keystore:Decrypt` to dsar-runner via ephemeral role for the rotation window, 3) run canary decrypt and smoke checks before cutover.
mike: + add an audit flag to attach KMS request-id to the DSAR evidence manifest so we can show the decrypt call in case of dispute.
sara: Legal ok with those mitigations. Also require an explicit reason in the audit ("key rotation - DSAR safety window").
raj: I'll prepare the canary script and the smoke check. Example craft: 
```
#!/bin/bash
for id in $(cat /tmp/canary_ids); do
  aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://$id --key-id alias/customer-data-prod || echo \"FAIL $id\"
done
```
jen: I'll add RBAC change as timebound in IAM: grant `keystore:Decrypt` to `role/dsar-runner-temporary` with `MaxSessionDuration=3600` and a 1-hour lifetime. We'll revoke after post-checks.
mike: I'll assemble pre-rotation export: list pending proof jobs, dsar ids, object paths, and push to secure bucket `s3://redwood-dsar-exports/rotation-pre-1809876543`.
sara: Please also update the DSAR incident policy to attach `dsar_id`, `requestor_email`, and `kms_request_id` to the evidence bundle. Privacy bot should tag the ticket.
privacy-bot: New DSAR incident policy note: tagging required: dsar_id, requestor_email, legal_ticket.
raj: Runbook checklist draft: 
- Pre-rotation export (owner: mike)
- Create ephemeral role and grant decrypt (owner: jen)
- Run canary decrypt (owner: raj)
- Perform key rotation (keystore team)
- Monitor `keystore.decrypt_denied` and `keystore.decrypt_ok` events (30m)
- Revoke ephemeral role (jen)
- Post-rotation verification & evidence upload (mike)
- Notify Legal & Privacy (sara)

mike: I'll add audit flag in deletion service to emit `kms_request_id` in the DSAR evidence manifest. That requires a small change in the service to plumb the value from keystore-proxy response. ETA 2h.
jen: I'll update runbook commands and add rollback snippet: 
```
# revoke temporary role
aws iam delete-role-policy --role-name dsar-runner-temporary --policy-name decrypt-allow
# restore previous IAM state from backup
```
raj: Also - retention exceptions: ensure any DSAR with a retention exception (legal hold) is not part of the export or deletion freeze logic. Mike, add filter: `retention_exception = true` -> skip.
mike: will do.
sara: Confirming timeline: start 2026-03-23T03:00:00Z, freeze window 15 minutes for rotation, monitor 30 minutes post-rotate. Legal approves.
raj: owners: raj (canary & monitoring), jen (RBAC + runbook), mike (exports + audit flag), sara (legal comm). I'll file the follow-up ticket and set reminders.
mike: quick question — who triggers pager if decrypt-denied spikes outside window? Should be eng-oncall + privacy.
raj: yes, alert rule: `sum(rate(keystore.decrypt_denied[5m])) > 5 -> page eng-oncall, privacy` with runbook link.
jen: I'll push the IAM change as a timebound policy and include CloudTrail retention for IAM events.
sara: No objections. Sounds good. Please post the ticket and tag @eng-oncall before executing. :thumbsup:
raj: will do.
